checks.claim: C1 object and hypotheses: J_h is well defined for every xi, every h in (0,1] and every ball-growth Radon measure, and the parameter ranges match H:homog with a=alpha_0.
checks.reason: The integrand is positive and continuous in lambda, so the integral is defined in [0,infinity], and eta=xi-lambda needs no density or Jacobian. Target lines 6-11 match canonical lines 7, 12 and 25-27. The gamma interval is nonempty because alpha+a<2 and a>0 force alpha<2. Riesz densities satisfy the hypothesis, and white noise is the alpha=d=1 case. C=0 forces nu=0.

checks.claim: C1 near region: for |lambda|<=4q with q=max(1,|xi|), dropping the brackets gives a bound uniform in xi and h and at most a constant times C B_alpha(h).
checks.reason: Here |eta|<=5q, and <xi> >= q gives <xi>^(2gamma-1)<=q^(2gamma-1) because 2gamma<1. Using balls centred at xi, the shell sum over |eta|<=5q is at most a constant times C for alpha<1, C(1+log q) for alpha=1, and C q^(alpha-1) for alpha>1. After the weight the powers are q^(2gamma-1), q^(2gamma-1)(1+log q), and q^(2gamma+alpha-2). All are bounded under the stated gamma range, and the log at alpha=1 is absorbed by the strict negative power. B_alpha>=1 on (0,1], so the near term fits the target.

checks.claim: C1 far region: for |lambda|>4q, centred shells give B_alpha(h), with tail summability exactly from alpha+a<2.
checks.reason: |xi|<|lambda|/4 gives 3|lambda|/4<=|eta|<=5|lambda|/4. It also gives ||xi|-|eta||>=|lambda|/2 and |xi|+|eta|>=|lambda|/2. The bracket is decreasing because a<1, and <x/2> >= <x>/2 lets the sum be written with <h2^j>^(a-1). Shells with h2^j<=1 give O(1), O(1+log(1/h)), or O(h^(1-alpha)). Shells with h2^j>1 give h^(a-1) times a geometric series in 2^(j(alpha+a-2)), which is O(h^(1-alpha))<=O(B_alpha). For |lambda|^(alpha-d)dlambda at xi=0, the integral converges iff alpha+a<2, so the word exactly is justified.
